issues.title: Ending apartment vacation rentals and hotel rezoning of 48 properties

recap.headline: Molokaʻi town hall weighs sites for a new County public cemetery
recap.in_60_seconds: Molokaʻi's Council office held its June town hall, mainly to hear the County Department of Public Works on finding a site for a new public cemetery. Kapaʻakea Cemetery, the island's only public cemetery, has only a few plots left. Public Works reviewed six sites, and the two top-ranked are both privately owned: the R.W. Meyer property near Kalaʻe and the Holomua Junction parcel. About 14 residents asked questions or commented, and most who stated a preference favored the Meyer site. The County has budgeted about $750,000; no site was chosen and no vote was taken. It is still unclear how long a new site would last, how big a buffer from homes would be, and what happens if Kapaʻakea fills first.

parts.title: Opening pule and agenda
presented: Meeting opened with pule.
Format: guest presentation, questions, then updates from groups, kept to about one hour.
Guests were the Public Works highway supervisor and the Molokaʻi district supervisor.

parts.title: Molokaʻi Cemetery Master Plan site search
parts.presenter: Department of Public Works highway supervisor
presented: A consultant screened state, County and private parcels of two acres or more and found six possible sites.
Sites were scored on environmental, social and cultural factors, site traits such as soils, water and power, and land use and zoning.

County and state agricultural parcels raised concerns about past pesticide use, water and fire risk; Holomua Junction may have contamination and has a large sewer line; the R.W. Meyer site has power, county water and willing owners.
Next step is to negotiate with landowners, then plan design, facilities and management.

next.what: Public Works to engage property owners about a purchase

parts.title: Questions on the cemetery sites
presented: The host said Kapaʻakea has about six plots left, with work underway to make room for about 10 more.
R.W. Meyer is about 8.5 acres; Holomua Junction is just under 15 acres.
About $750,000 is budgeted.

raised.concern: How much the private owners want for their land.
Effects on nearby homes at the Meyer site and how big a buffer would be.
Many Filipino families prefer burial over cremation and want loved ones buried together.
What happens if Kapaʻakea fills before a new cemetery is ready.
How many years a new site would serve the island.
Whether families could reserve the plot next to a loved one or bury spouses together.
A cemetery rules out other community uses of the land, such as commercial use or growing food.
Whether the public would be told before the County buys a site.
Sea level rise and the need to move burials to higher ground.
Holomua Junction lacks sewer and its water would cost far more than County water.

answered.said: Once an owner signs a letter of intent, the County Finance Department will appraise the land; past sales suggest it should fit the budget of about $750,000.
The Meyer parcel is large and wooded, so a buffer could be created; the buffer size is not known yet, and an environmental review will allow public comment.
If Kapaʻakea fills first, people would have to look to private cemeteries.
He has capacity figures and will send them through the Council office; he recalled roughly 50 to 200 years.
Plot reservations and other design and policy questions will be worked out after a property is acquired.
These meetings come first to gather community input before any purchase.
Moving burials because of sea level rise is being considered separately, such as setting aside a section for reinterment.

next.what: Public Works to send cemetery capacity estimates through the Council office
Environmental review with public comment on the chosen site

parts.title: Other site ideas and community preference
presented: The host asked for other site ideas and a general preference between Holomua Junction and the Meyer property, to pass on to Public Works.

raised.concern: Use land next to the existing Kapaʻakea cemetery.
Preference for the Meyer site near Kalaʻe as cooler, greener and park-like, near Pālāʻau State Park, versus an artificial green spot in arid Holomua; one resident praised the view from Holomua.
Urgency: only about two plots remain, and Molokaʻi still offers free public burial plots.

answered.said: Land near Kapaʻakea belongs to Hawaiian Home Lands, is leased, and sits low where sea level rise is a concern; food-growing areas were avoided.

parts.title: UH Maui College Molokaʻi Education Center update
presented: Newsletter mailed to all Molokaʻi Po boxes.
Grants for construction technology certificates, tuition-free first aid and CPR, and scholarships for health pathways.
Fall registration deadline is August 8; register in person at the campus.

parts.title: Commission updates
presented: The Commission on Healing Solutions for Homelessness meets online at 1:30 on the fourth Thursday of each month and advises the Council and administration.
It has made one recommendation so far, for a medical outreach unit, and wants district-specific plans for each of nine districts.
The Molokaʻi Planning Commission will review the resolution to end the Minatoya list for vacation rentals on July 10 at 11 a.m., online only.

next.what: Molokaʻi Planning Commission review of the Minatoya list resolution, online only

next.when: Fourth Thursday of each month at 1:30

parts.title: Community announcements
presented: The Community Health Center is seeking board members; applicants must be 18 and not have a family member working there.
The state representative highlighted a mailer summarizing the session.
Molokaʻi Heritage Trust visited tribes in California with the Lahaina Community Land Trust, is finishing bylaws, and aims to acquire about 56,000 acres of Molokaʻi Ranch land.
The next regatta is expected July 6 at 9 a.m. at the wharf; Molokaʻi Holokai is coming soon.

next.what: Molokaʻi Heritage Trust membership and board elections after bylaws

parts.title: Closing pule
presented: Meeting closed with pule.

bills.name: Molokaʻi Cemetery Master Plan
bills.what: County Public Works plan to choose, buy, design and manage a new public cemetery on Molokaʻi.

bills.name: Resolution to end the Minatoya list
bills.what: Would end the list allowing nonconforming vacation rental uses in apartment-zoned buildings.

open_questions.question: How many years would the R.W. Meyer or Holomua Junction site serve Molokaʻi?
How large would the buffer be between a cemetery and nearby homes at the Meyer site?
What will families do if Kapaʻakea fills before a new cemetery opens?
What price would the private owners accept for their land?

not_on_tracker.topic: New County public cemetery for Molokaʻi
not_on_tracker.why: The island's only public cemetery is nearly full, and residents want free public burial close to home.
The commission chair says it needs community support and a district-specific approach to help Molokaʻi.

not_on_tracker.topic: Molokaʻi Heritage Trust effort to acquire Molokaʻi Ranch lands
not_on_tracker.why: A community-led trust hopes to return about 56,000 acres to community control.
The health center is in transition and needs community members on its board.

moments.who: Chair of the Molokaʻi Planning Commission
moments.quote: The second thing coming up is July 10th, we Molokaʻi will be reviewing the resolution to end the Minatoa list for non-conforming uses of things that were set back before when it comes to vacation rentals. So there are over 900 people in attendance yesterday in the Maui Planning Commission.
moments.about: Gives the Molokaʻi Planning Commission's July 10 online-only review date for the proposal to end Minatoya-list vacation rentals and notes the large turnout at the Maui Planning Commission hearing.
